title: Cardbook not working

content:
starting yesterday, I can not edit old contacts or add new ones to cardbook. when I click on either the edit or new contact tab at the top of the cardbook screen or do a right click on the contact and select edit, It takes me to a blank new contact entry form for the thunderbird contacts, not the old cardbook file. Also, when I tried to send information to the cardbook support or went to their .uci page, both returned the error message that the address did not exist.

so I am wondering if cardbook is now dead and I need to load all my contact into thunderbirds contacts, or if there is some simple fix that I am ignorant of.

I loved cardbook, have well over a thousand contacts, old customers and vendors add up quickly, and cardbook gave me the ability to better organize them with sub groups so they were easy to find by specific trade. I did not see that capability in older versions of the thunderbird contacts.

title: Move to > Recent folder results in hierarchy problem
creator: alysenet1
content:

title: Where is my address book?
creator: victorhart
content: I have had very few notices about Thunderbird upgrades. My records show Setup numbers: 3.0.exe, 8.0.exe, 52.4.0.exe, 52.9.1.exe, 78.12.0.exe, and then 115.5.2.exe. My address book made it through all but the last upgrade. No notice that I should save a copy of my address book ever showed up in any correspondence. I tried reinstalling an old upgrade but the upgrade always wants to update the installation. I did try to reinstall 52.9.1, but the next screen wanted my name and password. It would not accept any name and password that I could remember. So I tried searching for them at Xfinity and Comcast to no result. I did not try my Firefox password because it didn't seem appropriate. Incidentally, my records show 135 upgrades for Firefox for the same length of time as the upgrades for Thunderbird. My fear is that my address book is unrecoverable. I chose Thunderbird because I ofigured none of it would need backup if it became necessary to reinstall Windows 10. Which happened last year. I did not expect Mozilla to change Thunderbird so drastically that I couldn't get every thing back. Sorry but I'm a senior citizen and not computer literate. If I have to try to recreate my address book I may as well use Microsoft's Outlook as it looks somewhat simpler than Thunderbird - which I doubt.
